title: [Cr(CO)<sub>6</sub>]
sheetLabel: Elements to list (point group not required)
note: 48 operations. Same symmetry as the paper octahedron from Lab 2: each Cr–C≡O unit is straight, so the ligands behave like octahedron vertices. Labels sit on the O atoms; the C moves with its O.

classes.label: C<sub>4</sub>
moves: CO<sub>2</sub>→CO<sub>3</sub>→CO<sub>4</sub>→CO<sub>5</sub>. Cr, CO<sub>1</sub>, CO<sub>6</sub> stay put.
CO<sub>1</sub>→CO<sub>2</sub>→CO<sub>6</sub>→CO<sub>4</sub>. Cr, CO<sub>3</sub>, CO<sub>5</sub> stay put.
CO<sub>1</sub>→CO<sub>5</sub>→CO<sub>6</sub>→CO<sub>3</sub>. Cr, CO<sub>2</sub>, CO<sub>4</sub> stay put.

classes.label: C<sub>3</sub>
moves: CO<sub>1</sub>→CO<sub>2</sub>→CO<sub>3</sub>; CO<sub>4</sub>→CO<sub>5</sub>→CO<sub>6</sub>. Cr stays put.
CO<sub>1</sub>→CO<sub>5</sub>→CO<sub>2</sub>; CO<sub>3</sub>→CO<sub>4</sub>→CO<sub>6</sub>. Cr stays put.
CO<sub>1</sub>→CO<sub>4</sub>→CO<sub>3</sub>; CO<sub>2</sub>→CO<sub>5</sub>→CO<sub>6</sub>. Cr stays put.
CO<sub>1</sub>→CO<sub>5</sub>→CO<sub>4</sub>; CO<sub>2</sub>→CO<sub>6</sub>→CO<sub>3</sub>. Cr stays put.

classes.label: C<sub>2</sub>′
moves: CO<sub>1</sub>↔CO<sub>2</sub>; CO<sub>3</sub>↔CO<sub>5</sub>; CO<sub>4</sub>↔CO<sub>6</sub>. Cr stays put.
CO<sub>1</sub>↔CO<sub>3</sub>; CO<sub>2</sub>↔CO<sub>4</sub>; CO<sub>5</sub>↔CO<sub>6</sub>. Cr stays put.
CO<sub>1</sub>↔CO<sub>4</sub>; CO<sub>2</sub>↔CO<sub>6</sub>; CO<sub>3</sub>↔CO<sub>5</sub>. Cr stays put.
CO<sub>1</sub>↔CO<sub>5</sub>; CO<sub>2</sub>↔CO<sub>4</sub>; CO<sub>3</sub>↔CO<sub>6</sub>. Cr stays put.
CO<sub>1</sub>↔CO<sub>6</sub>; CO<sub>2</sub>↔CO<sub>3</sub>; CO<sub>4</sub>↔CO<sub>5</sub>. Cr stays put.
CO<sub>1</sub>↔CO<sub>6</sub>; CO<sub>2</sub>↔CO<sub>5</sub>; CO<sub>3</sub>↔CO<sub>4</sub>. Cr stays put.

classes.label: i
classes.what: Send each atom through Cr to the other side
moves: CO<sub>1</sub>↔CO<sub>6</sub>; CO<sub>2</sub>↔CO<sub>4</sub>; CO<sub>3</sub>↔CO<sub>5</sub>. Cr stays put.

classes.label: S<sub>4</sub>
classes.what: Turn 90°, then reflect through the plane ⟂ to the line
moves: CO<sub>1</sub>↔CO<sub>6</sub>; CO<sub>2</sub>→CO<sub>3</sub>→CO<sub>4</sub>→CO<sub>5</sub>. Cr stays put.
CO<sub>1</sub>→CO<sub>2</sub>→CO<sub>6</sub>→CO<sub>4</sub>; CO<sub>3</sub>↔CO<sub>5</sub>. Cr stays put.
CO<sub>1</sub>→CO<sub>5</sub>→CO<sub>6</sub>→CO<sub>3</sub>; CO<sub>2</sub>↔CO<sub>4</sub>. Cr stays put.

classes.label: S<sub>6</sub>
classes.what: Turn 60°, then reflect through the plane ⟂ to the line
moves: CO<sub>1</sub>→CO<sub>5</sub>→CO<sub>2</sub>→CO<sub>6</sub>→CO<sub>3</sub>→CO<sub>4</sub>. Cr stays put.
CO<sub>1</sub>→CO<sub>4</sub>→CO<sub>5</sub>→CO<sub>6</sub>→CO<sub>2</sub>→CO<sub>3</sub>. Cr stays put.
CO<sub>1</sub>→CO<sub>5</sub>→CO<sub>4</sub>→CO<sub>6</sub>→CO<sub>3</sub>→CO<sub>2</sub>. Cr stays put.
CO<sub>1</sub>→CO<sub>2</sub>→CO<sub>5</sub>→CO<sub>6</sub>→CO<sub>4</sub>→CO<sub>3</sub>. Cr stays put.

classes.label: σ<sub>h</sub>
moves: CO<sub>1</sub>↔CO<sub>6</sub>. Cr, CO<sub>2</sub>, CO<sub>3</sub>, CO<sub>4</sub>, CO<sub>5</sub> stay put.
CO<sub>3</sub>↔CO<sub>5</sub>. Cr, CO<sub>1</sub>, CO<sub>2</sub>, CO<sub>4</sub>, CO<sub>6</sub> stay put.
CO<sub>2</sub>↔CO<sub>4</sub>. Cr, CO<sub>1</sub>, CO<sub>3</sub>, CO<sub>5</sub>, CO<sub>6</sub> stay put.

classes.label: σ<sub>d</sub>
moves: CO<sub>1</sub>↔CO<sub>4</sub>; CO<sub>2</sub>↔CO<sub>6</sub>. Cr, CO<sub>3</sub>, CO<sub>5</sub> stay put.
CO<sub>1</sub>↔CO<sub>5</sub>; CO<sub>3</sub>↔CO<sub>6</sub>. Cr, CO<sub>2</sub>, CO<sub>4</sub> stay put.
CO<sub>1</sub>↔CO<sub>2</sub>; CO<sub>4</sub>↔CO<sub>6</sub>. Cr, CO<sub>3</sub>, CO<sub>5</sub> stay put.
CO<sub>1</sub>↔CO<sub>3</sub>; CO<sub>5</sub>↔CO<sub>6</sub>. Cr, CO<sub>2</sub>, CO<sub>4</sub> stay put.
CO<sub>2</sub>↔CO<sub>5</sub>; CO<sub>3</sub>↔CO<sub>4</sub>. Cr, CO<sub>1</sub>, CO<sub>6</sub> stay put.
CO<sub>2</sub>↔CO<sub>3</sub>; CO<sub>4</sub>↔CO<sub>5</sub>. Cr, CO<sub>1</sub>, CO<sub>6</sub> stay put.

classes.label: Try C<sub>6</sub> on a C<sub>3</sub> line
classes.msg: Looking down this line you see six ligands in a zig-zag, three up and three down. A plain 60° turn puts an up-ligand where a down-ligand was: not a symmetry operation. Add a reflection and it works: that is the S6.

classes.label: Try C<sub>8</sub> (45°)
classes.msg: The four equatorial ligands land between their old positions: not a symmetry operation. The smallest turn that works about this line is 90°.

walk.q: Two or more C<sub>3</sub> (or higher) axes?
walk.detail: Several high-order axes: a T<sub>d</sub>, O<sub>h</sub> or I<sub>h</sub> shape.
Order 48. Students are not asked for this label.

title: Naphthalene C<sub>10</sub>H<sub>8</sub>
sheetLabel: Elements to list (point group not required)
sheet: E, C2(z), C2(y), C2(x), i, σ(xy), σ(xz), σ(yz)
note: 8 operations. Same point group as B<sub>2</sub>H<sub>6</sub> in Lab 2. x = long axis, y = short axis through C<sub>4a</sub> and C<sub>8a</sub>, z = ⟂ to the ring plane. Each H moves with its C.

classes.label: C<sub>2</sub>(z)
classes.what: Turn 180° about the line ⟂ to the ring plane
moves: C<sub>1</sub>↔C<sub>5</sub>; C<sub>2</sub>↔C<sub>6</sub>; C<sub>3</sub>↔C<sub>7</sub>; C<sub>4</sub>↔C<sub>8</sub>; C<sub>4a</sub>↔C<sub>8a</sub>. No atom stays put. Each H moves with its C.

classes.label: C<sub>2</sub>(y)
classes.what: Turn 180° about the short axis (through C<sub>4a</sub>, C<sub>8a</sub>)
moves: C<sub>1</sub>↔C<sub>8</sub>; C<sub>2</sub>↔C<sub>7</sub>; C<sub>3</sub>↔C<sub>6</sub>; C<sub>4</sub>↔C<sub>5</sub>. C<sub>4a</sub>, C<sub>8a</sub> stay put. Each H moves with its C.

classes.label: C<sub>2</sub>(x)
classes.what: Turn 180° about the long axis (no atoms on it)
moves: C<sub>1</sub>↔C<sub>4</sub>; C<sub>2</sub>↔C<sub>3</sub>; C<sub>4a</sub>↔C<sub>8a</sub>; C<sub>5</sub>↔C<sub>8</sub>; C<sub>6</sub>↔C<sub>7</sub>. No atom stays put. Each H moves with its C.

classes.label: i
classes.what: Send each atom through the centre of the C<sub>4a</sub>–C<sub>8a</sub> bond
moves: C<sub>1</sub>↔C<sub>5</sub>; C<sub>2</sub>↔C<sub>6</sub>; C<sub>3</sub>↔C<sub>7</sub>; C<sub>4</sub>↔C<sub>8</sub>; C<sub>4a</sub>↔C<sub>8a</sub>. No atom stays put. Each H moves with its C.

classes.label: σ(xy)
moves: Every atom stays put: the plane contains the whole molecule. It still counts as an operation; it swaps the top and bottom faces of the ring. C<sub>1</sub>, C<sub>2</sub>, C<sub>3</sub>, C<sub>4</sub>, C<sub>4a</sub>, C<sub>5</sub>, C<sub>6</sub>, C<sub>7</sub>, C<sub>8</sub>, C<sub>8a</sub> stay put.

classes.label: σ(xz)
classes.what: Reflect through the plane ⟂ to the ring, along the long axis
moves: C<sub>1</sub>↔C<sub>4</sub>; C<sub>2</sub>↔C<sub>3</sub>; C<sub>4a</sub>↔C<sub>8a</sub>; C<sub>5</sub>↔C<sub>8</sub>; C<sub>6</sub>↔C<sub>7</sub>. No atom stays put. Each H moves with its C.

classes.label: σ(yz)
classes.what: Reflect through the plane ⟂ to the ring, through C<sub>4a</sub> and C<sub>8a</sub>
moves: C<sub>1</sub>↔C<sub>8</sub>; C<sub>2</sub>↔C<sub>7</sub>; C<sub>3</sub>↔C<sub>6</sub>; C<sub>4</sub>↔C<sub>5</sub>. C<sub>4a</sub>, C<sub>8a</sub> stay put. Each H moves with its C.

classes.label: Try C<sub>6</sub> (benzene thinking)
classes.what: Turn 60° about the line ⟂ to the plane
classes.msg: Each ring alone looks like benzene, but the molecule is two rings side by side. A 60° turn swings the long axis out of line: not a symmetry operation. Only the 180° turn about this line works.

classes.label: Try C<sub>2</sub> through C<sub>1</sub> and C<sub>5</sub>
classes.what: Turn 180° about the diagonal line through C<sub>1</sub> and C<sub>5</sub>
classes.msg: C1 and C5 stay, but the rest of the molecule swings out of place: not a symmetry operation. The in-plane C2 axes run along the long and short directions only.

walk.q: Two or more C<sub>3</sub> (or higher) axes?

walk.detail: Three C<sub>2</sub> axes tie; take the one ⟂ to the plane as main. Hold it vertical.
Order 8. Students are not asked for this label.
